solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

parts.note: to second a motion or a person is to back them
a bit is the metal mouthpiece of a horse's bridle

explanation.surface: Someone speaking indistinctly, helped along by a second microphone or mouthpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slurred' pretends to mean mumbled speech; here it means spoke ill of someone behind their back.
explanation.definitionFit: To backbite is to malign someone in their absence, so slurred in the sense of smeared is its past tense.

definitions.meaning: a disreputable member of a family or group
a stale or rotten egg floats in water, the old kitchen freshness test

explanation.surface: A wayward family member is pictured bobbing on water.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a rogue, and literally an off egg, which floats when tested in a bowl of water.

clue.text: Sound of Hoy youths keeping you confused with frequently asked questions

indicators.note: one word keeping others holds them within itself, so the young men's word is split open around them

parts.note: youths are boys

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: F begins frequently: the three words together abbreviate to FAQ, the familiar initialism for a help list
A is the initial of asked, the middle letter of FAQ
Q is the initial of questions, the last letter of FAQ

explanation.surface: Young people on the Orkney island of Hoy, baffled, are fielding a list of common queries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like a noise but is a sea inlet. Hoy is one of the Orkney islands off northern Scotland, and FAQ is the initialism of 'frequently asked questions'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bay of Quoys is an inlet of Hoy, and a sound is a stretch of sea water, so it is a body of water there.

clue.text: All criticism aired before half time

parts.note: tut is the clicking noise voiced in disapproval

indicators.note: half of the four-letter word time is its opening pair of letters

explanation.surface: A pundit voices criticism just before the half-time whistle.
explanation.definitionFit: In music tutti is an instruction for every performer to play together.

definitions.meaning: a wild crab apple tree or its fruit
the suffragette at 18 was named Emily ... Davison, so her middle name sits inside her full name

explanation.surface: Something has been gulped down by whoever is at 18.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild apple tree is called this, and it is also the middle name of the suffragette in the grid.

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of two words here trade places

parts.note: drawn tight is taut
a polished surface may be waxy

explanation.surface: Spooner has sketched a gleaming boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'taut a waxy' and swap the opening consonants to hear 'waught a taxy'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small boat carrying paying passengers across water works as a ferry.

definitions.meaning: told a fib, said something untrue
a German art song, as by Schubert

explanation.surface: A tale recounted through song, like a ballad.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling a story can mean fibbing, and the German word for an art song shares the spelling.

definitions.meaning: lives in, occupies as a home
monks dress in robes called habits, so they live clothed in them

explanation.surface: A description of monastic life.
explanation.definitionFit: To occupy a place as a dweller is to live there; split in two, it describes monks wearing robes.

clue.text: Messing about with a high meat quality

indicators.note: letters knocked about are thrown into disorder, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone fooling around with a well-hung piece of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Messing about' is a phrase, but 'about' is the anagram signal and 'Messing' plus 'a' is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Game hung until strongly flavoured is called high, and that strong taste is its gaminess.

definitions.meaning: belonging to a city of the English Midlands
the American name for a bowler hat

explanation.surface: A cricketer who bowls for a Midlands side.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a cricket bowler from the Midlands, the central region of England; in fact it is the hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Derby is a Midlands city, and Americans call a bowler hat by the same name.

clue.text: Rough anchor treatment produced bend, of course

indicators.note: rough treatment of letters knocks them into a new order

explanation.surface: Handling an anchor roughly has caused it to bend.
explanation.walkthrough: The course is Epsom racecourse, home of the Derby; Tattenham Corner is its famous turn into the home straight, where Emily Davison was struck by the King's horse in 1913.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the sharp turn on Epsom racecourse, literally a bend on a course.

indicators.note: the brothers come after the word for old

parts.note: grey hair goes with old age, so grey can mean old
friars are brothers of a religious order

explanation.surface: Monks trail behind an ancient educational institution.
explanation.definitionFit: Greyfriars is the fictional boarding school of Billy Bunter in Frank Richards' stories.

clue.text: After returning honour, name is black

indicators.note: the abbreviation for name is placed after the turned honour
returning means the letters for the honour are read backwards

parts.note: the OBE, Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.surface: Someone takes back an award, and their name is blackened.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebon is a poetic word for the dark colour of ebony wood.

parts.note: reads as a burglar alarm tripped by intruders, but describes the fear that foreigners provoke

explanation.surface: Intruders have triggered a security alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fear or hatred of foreigners: the Greek elements mean stranger and fear.

clue.text: Lacking energy, brave time to return home to badger protestors

indicators.note: lacking energy means the word for brave goes without its E

parts.note: to brave something is to suffer or endure it
E is the physics symbol for energy
an age is a period of time

indicators.note: to return means the badger's home is read backwards

parts.note: a sett is a badger's burrow

explanation.surface: Exhausted, someone must face the time to go home and pester the demonstrators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lacking' removes E from SUFFER to leave SUFFR; 'to return' turns SETT into TTES.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffragettes were women campaigning militantly in early twentieth-century Britain for the vote.

clue.text: Out-of-date belief of late arthouse characters

indicators.note: the characters are the letters of the three words, among which the answer runs

explanation.surface: An outmoded idea held by the people in recent art films.
explanation.definitionFit: The notion that the world is not round is the archetypal discredited belief.

clue.text: Feeble Roundhead and Parliamentarian's first appearing individually in fraud

indicators.note: in places the second opening letter inside the word for fraud as well
each of the two letters goes into the word for fraud separately, at different places

parts.note: deceit is fraud or trickery
the 'first' serves both soldiers: Roundhead's first letter is R

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A weak Cromwellian soldier and politician turn up one at a time in a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: R and P go into DECEIT one at a time: DEC-R-E-P-IT. Roundheads were Parliament's side in the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: Decrepit means worn out and weakened by age, so feeble is a close synonym.

clue.text: Pet abandoned by poorly painted goal line between corners

indicators.note: the letters of the pet word are left out of the pool
poorly arranged letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A dog left behind by a shoddily decorated goal line.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove P, E, T from PAINTEDGOAL, and 'poorly' rearranges the remaining AINDGOAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagonal is a straight line joining opposite vertices of a shape.

indicators.note: letters handled carelessly fall out of order and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A diplomat has been carelessly lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Emily Davison was a militant campaigner for votes for women, killed at the 1913 Derby.

clue.text: Suspended former right of president to refuse intake

parts.note: suspended means hung up
erst is an old word for formerly
Ike was the nickname of US president Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A former presidential prerogative to decline something has been suspended.
explanation.definitionFit: A protest in which someone refuses food is a refusal of intake, a fast used as a weapon.

indicators.note: the possessive reads as has: the answer at 14 has the four letters inside it

parts.note: the answer at 14 is the word for the women campaigners

explanation.surface: A protestor's angry tirade.
explanation.definitionFit: To rage is to shout furiously, the same sense as a rant.

clue.text: From Paris, I send message about German building vapour trail

parts.note: je is French for I

indicators.note: the message word goes about, around, the building word

parts.note: to text is to send a message by phone
Haus is German for house

explanation.surface: A French speaker texts about a German construction project.
explanation.definitionFit: The visible trail behind an aircraft is condensed vapour from its jet exhaust.

indicators.note: an extract is a section taken out of a passage, here a run of these words

explanation.surface: Stopping plans to copy a passage from a text.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, to estop is to bar a party from asserting something, so it means to prevent.

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a tie is a link or association

explanation.surface: An Asian society has been publicly declared.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Thailand is an Asian national.

indicators.note: sabotage wrecks the order of the letters, which are rebuilt

explanation.surface: Militant protestors disrupting a search for a spark.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmeline Pankhurst and her daughters Christabel and Sylvia led the suffragette movement.

clue.text: Is talk reverting to childish claim?

indicators.note: reverting means the pair of words is read from the back

parts.note: gab is chatter or talk

explanation.surface: Is this conversation sliding back into infantile squabbling?
explanation.definitionFit: Children shout this phrase to claim first right to something, like a front seat.

indicators.note: the hard abbreviation comes after the composer's name

parts.note: Thomas Tallis was an English Tudor composer
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A composer whose music is difficult to grasp has a lofty style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard-to-follow' reads as obscure, but splits as H, then 'to follow'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallish means rather tall, so it is a mild way of saying fairly high up.

indicators.note: the publicity abbreviation comes before the rest

parts.note: PR is public relations, publicity
an air is a song or tune
i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A promotional push before a song, and that's that, plain and simple.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a wide grassy plain, as in North America.
